correctness.rationale: The standard edge-segment support-function width is exactly total variation. Nested level-set coarea and the strict Euclidean triangle-equality case reduce all minimizers to individual centered cuts. Cutting a one-hub cycle–star graph leaves only one-leaf cuts or nonhub contiguous arcs optimal, with strict inequalities excluding mixed cuts and multi-run cuts. Exact quadratic optimization determines both widths and equality classes; the increasing cut-balance ratio proves the entire phase diagram. Exact independent brute-force cut checks cover 63 finite parameter cases, plus 9800 threshold checks. This finite corroboration is not used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: A cycle with a bunched pendant star is a structurally natural unicyclic graph family. Its minimum Euclidean width has two competing geometric mechanisms: one bridge cut and two-edge connected cycle arcs. The complete exact equality-case classification reveals a seven-family universal 15-vertex resonance and two exceptional higher-order ties, not just a direct variable substitution into the known variational formula. This supplies a testable natural sharp metric invariant and phase diagram for a canonical polytope family.
